name: About
description: Page header, manifesto text with emphasized lines, principles list, name + open-source notes.

fields.p1: WordPress made publishing easy in 2003. It's now 2026. The web has changed; the CMS hasn't.
fields.p2: We built Squilla because the existing options force a choice: be developer-friendly OR be content-editor-friendly. Be fast OR be flexible. Be open-source OR be AI-ready. Squilla refuses the trade.

items.body: Not as a "ChatGPT integration." As primary operators with the same API surface humans use.
items.heading: AI agents are first-class users.

items.body: Sub-50ms TTFB on every public page. Always.
items.heading: Performance is non-negotiable.

items.body: If disabling a feature would leave dead code in core, that feature belongs in an extension.
items.heading: The kernel stays small.

items.body: Their tables, their UI, their scripts, their migrations. The kernel doesn't reach inside.
items.heading: Extensions are sovereign.

items.body: docker compose up and you're publishing. No package managers, no cron jobs, no PHP-FPM tuning.
items.heading: One-shot setup.

fields.os_body: GPL-3.0. No telemetry. No CLA. No "open core" bait-and-switch. What's in the repo is the whole thing.
fields.name_body: Squilla is the Latin genus of mantis shrimps — the fastest punchers in the animal kingdom (sub-millisecond strike) and possessing the most complex visual system on Earth (16 photoreceptor types vs. our 3). Extreme speed; multi-spectrum perception (for AI agents); a segmented body with specialized appendages (kernel + extensions). The metaphor wrote itself.
